questions.prompt: If EffectDspVolumeUpdate internally encounters an error and returns a non-SUCCESS code, what does EffectVolumeUpdateInner return to its caller?

options.label: The error code from EffectDspVolumeUpdate
ERROR, because a volume update failed
SUCCESS — the return values of both inner calls are discarded

questions.explanation: The function calls EffectDspVolumeUpdate and EffectApVolumeUpdate but does not capture or check their return values. It unconditionally returns SUCCESS regardless of whether either inner function failed. The old code branched between DSP and AP based on offload state; the new code calls both and ignores their results.
questions.reinforce: Correct — both return values are discarded and SUCCESS is always returned.

questions.prompt: If deviceTypeToSystemVolumeMap_ has no entry for the requested deviceType AND no entry for DEVICE_TYPE_SPEAKER, what value is returned?

questions.prompt: The old code iterated sceneTypeToSessionIDMap_ and returned ERROR if a session's effect chain key was missing from sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_. In this new code, what happens to sessions that exist in sceneTypeToSessionIDMap_ but have no corresponding entry in sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_?

options.label: The function returns ERROR for those sessions, same as before
Those sessions are silently skipped — the loop iterates sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_ directly, so sessions without chains are never visited
A new effect chain is created on the fly for the missing session

questions.explanation: The new loop iterates sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_ (the chain map) rather than sceneTypeToSessionIDMap_ (the session map). Sessions that exist but have no corresponding chain entry are simply never encountered by the loop — no ERROR is raised for them. This is a behavioral change from the old code which would fail hard on any session lacking a chain.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the loop is now chain-centric, not session-centric.
